newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of August 11, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.
PC WEEK - Sun Microsystems Inc is taking a more direct path to running its Java programming language on Windows, and is no longer relying on Microsoft Corp, PC Week reported August 11.
Sun's strategy includes the formation of a direct sales force, deals with PC makers and the creation of a Java client/server product that will run on top of windows.

Intranet search engines are becoming more useful tools because of advancements in the past six months, PC Week reported August 11, including support for different kinds of data, open database connectivity compliance and the ability to give more control to network administrators.

COMPUTERWORLD - Computer companies are being forced to turn away customers because of the strike against United Parcel Service of America Inc, Computerworld reported August 11. Companies' package-processing systems are being stretched beyond their limits.

Federal Express upgraded two of its file transfer protocal services from T1 to T3 connections, giving it 28 times more capacity to handle World Wide Web visitors tracking shipments and placing orders online, Computerworld reported Aug. 11.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Apple Computer Inc's $150 million transfusion from archrival Microsoft Corp comes as the computer company plans behind the scenes to cut off its Mac OS licesnees, Computer Reseller News reported August 11.

Uncertainty over the clone situation and its overall channel strategy continue to plague the company and Apple is said to be considering build-to-order and direct efforts, sources told Computer Reseller News.

INFOWORLD - A proposed single "Device Bay" specification to allow equipment such as CD-ROM drives to be swapped among desktop and laptop computers is collapsing, InfoWorld reported Aug. 11. The plan was backed by Microsoft Corp, Intel Corp and Compaq Computer Inc.

Microsoft's $150 million investment in Apple Computer Inc is likely to diminsh the Internet influence of Netscape Communications Corp over the next several years, InfoWorld reported Aug. 11 in a news analysis.

INFORMATION WEEK - SAP AG will unveil a set of supply-chain management applications this month and has entered the Internet commerce market as the fourth-largest software maker lowers the entry price point for midsize companies, Information Week reported August 11.
Tandem Computers Inc is set to announce the availability of the first Windows NT system that runs on Microsoft Cluster software, formerly known as Wolfpack, Information Week reported Aug. 11.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Wyle Electronics Inc got a new owner and chief executive last week when Raab Karcher AG completed its acquistiion of the distributor and immeidately installed one of its own executives, Michael Rohleder, to head the company, EBN reported August 11.

EE TIMES - Sun Microsystems's bid to reshape its Java programming language into a mainstay of the embedded computing world is raising concerns among developers of real-time software applications, according to industry analysts, EE Times reported August 11. Sun plans to unveil the specifications for Embedded Java, next month, EE Times said.

Mentor Graphics Corp attempt to enter the logic emulation business suffered a double blow when QuickTurn Design Systems Inc of Mountain View, Calif. won two court decisions this month, EE TImes reported August 11.

MACWEEK - Relations between Apple Computer and its licensees hit a new low as the aggrieved parties skirmished in public last week at the MacWorld Expo, with systems vendors saying that Apple was turning its back on licensing, MacWeek reported August 11.

Many show goers at MacWorld said they were disappointed by the absence of some companies whose products run on the Mac, including Macromedia Inc, Iomega Corp and America Online Inc MacWeek reported August 11.
